meta.document: F51 Darwin-X Mission Control — Dashboard Component Specification

stack.transport: Server-Sent Events (SSE) — single persistent connection, auto-reconnect
stack.storage: SQLite WAL (metrics, gpu_snapshots, checkpoint_history) + in-memory deques (maxlen=7200) for live charts
stack.dependencies: 2 new pip deps: fastapi, uvicorn (~25MB). Zero npm, zero node, zero build step.

tier_fast.description: Training metrics, GPU stats, loss/dopamine live values

tier_slow.description: SHA-256 fingerprints, organ status grid, agent timeline

data_pipeline.overview: Training process writes files to disk. Dashboard backend polls files every 2s via asyncio loop, reads mtime+size to detect changes, parses new data, pushes deltas to browser via SSE. Browser maintains in-memory deques for chart history (client-side buffer, last 1000 points per chart). SQLite WAL stores historical metrics for persistence across dashboard restarts.

DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md.format: Markdown with structured sections (ESTADO ATUAL table, agent entry/exit blocks)

sse_event_types.metrics: Fast-tier payload: loss, ppl, tok_s, jepa, dopamine, delta, gmc, cycle, step, gpu[]
sse_event_types.blockchain: Medium-tier payload: block_count, head_hash, last_cycle, blockchain_status
sse_event_types.system: Medium-tier payload: ram_pct, disk_pct, proc_count, uptime, gpu_temp[]
sse_event_types.organs: Slow-tier payload: organ_states[] (16 entries with name, status, identity_short)
sse_event_types.timeline: Slow-tier payload: entries[] (timestamp, agent, operation_type, summary)
sse_event_types.heartbeat: Every 15s: server timestamp — used for staleness detection client-side

logbook_integration.parser: Regex-based parser in Python backend. Reads DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md on mtime change.
logbook_integration.estado_atual_table: Parses the markdown table under '## ESTADO ATUAL' section into dict. Provides checkpoint state, git commit, training status, organ count, blockchain status.
logbook_integration.agent_entries: Parses timestamped blocks with OPERATION, ESTADO ENCONTRADO, AÇÕES, ESTADO DEIXADO. Extracts agent name, operation type (READ/WRITE/EXECUTE/DECIDE/MIXED), and first-line summary.
logbook_integration.bugs_section: Parses numbered bug list under '## Bugs conhecidos'. Each bug: id, title, status.
logbook_integration.dashboard_writes: Dashboard APPENDS training start/stop events and periodic snapshots (every 100 steps) to DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md via advisory file lock (msvcrt.locking on Windows) with 2s timeout + pending queue.
logbook_integration.cache: agent_timeline.json in workspace/runtime/dashboard/ — regenerated on DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md mtime change.

HeroLoss.name: HeroLoss
HeroLoss.purpose: Dominant focal element showing the current training loss value with trend direction. The most visually prominent element on the dashboard — loss is the single most important metric for training health.

data_sources.primary: dopamine_status.txt → key 'loss' (total loss) and 'lm_loss' (language modeling baseline)
data_sources.trend_comparison: Previous value stored in client-side deque (last 2 seconds)

loading.visual: Pulsing placeholder rectangle (CSS animation: opacity 0.3→0.6→0.3, 1.5s cycle). Width: 200px, height: 48px.

live.visual: Large numeric value (font: Cascadia Code, 56px, weight 700, color #e0e0e0). Trend arrow to the right (24px). Value formatted to 4 decimal places.
live.label: Small 'LOSS' label above number (font: Inter, 12px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em, color #888888)

stale.condition: No SSE 'metrics' event received for > 30 seconds
stale.visual: Number remains but opacity drops to 0.4. Yellow warning badge 'STALE' appears top-right of card (font: Inter, 10px, bg #ffc107, text #0d0d0d).

error.condition: dopamine_status.txt missing, unparseable, or contains NaN/Inf
error.visual: Red dashed outline on card (2px #ff1744). Text shows '--' in red. Tooltip on hover: 'Data source error: <reason>'.

training_stopped.visual: Gray overlay on card. Number dimmed to #555555. Badge 'STOPPED' (bg #333333, text #888888) replaces trend arrow.

edge_cases.loss_is_zero: Display '0.0000' normally — zero loss is valid during very early warmup. Trend arrow shows ◆ (flat) since comparison may also be zero.
edge_cases.loss_is_negative: Display the value in red with warning tooltip: 'Negative loss — possible numerical instability'.
edge_cases.loss_nan_or_inf: Display 'NaN' or '∞' in red. Card gets error state (red dashed outline). SSE emits 'error' event with detail.
edge_cases.loss_above_100: Display the value normally but with yellow warning tint on the number. High loss during warmup steps is expected.
edge_cases.first_ever_value: No trend arrow shown (no previous value to compare). Display '--' as trend until second data point arrives.
edge_cases.rapid_change: If |delta| > 1.0 between 2s samples, flash the number background briefly (200ms, color based on direction: green flash for decreasing, red flash for increasing) to draw attention.

visual_behavior.transition: Number updates use CSS transition (color 0.3s ease). No morphing/animation on the number itself — instant numeric update to avoid disorientation.
visual_behavior.color_change: If loss drops by >0.01, number briefly pulses green (box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(0,230,118,0.4), 500ms, then fades). If loss spikes by >0.05, number briefly pulses red.
visual_behavior.tooltip: Hovering the number shows a tooltip: 'lm_loss: X.XXXX | aux_loss: X.XXXX | total_loss: X.XXXX' (breakdown).
visual_behavior.responsive: On viewport < 900px, font size drops to 36px. Trend arrow moves below number.

HeroLoss.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'metrics'. Field: 'loss'. Client extracts loss value, computes trend vs stored previous value, updates DOM element #hero-loss.

CycleStepChip.name: CycleStepChip
CycleStepChip.purpose: Compact badges showing current training cycle and step numbers, with a progress bar indicating step completion within the current cycle (500 steps per cycle for 100M). Also shows the checkpoint-saved cycle/step for comparison.

data_sources.cycle_length: Hardcoded 500 for 100M lineage (configurable via config endpoint)

loading.visual: Two pulsing chips (80x28px each) with shimmer animation. Progress bar hidden.

live.visual: Two adjacent chips: Cycle badge (bg #1a1a1a, border 1px #00d4ff, text cyan) and Step badge (bg #1a1a1a, border 1px #00d4ff, text cyan). Font: Cascadia Code, 14px.
live.progress_bar: Horizontal bar below chips (width: 100%, height: 3px, bg #333333). Fill portion = (step % 500) / 500, color #00d4ff. Shows intra-cycle progress.
live.checkpoint_indicator: Green dot (8px) appears left of Cycle chip when step == checkpoint step (synced). Yellow dot when step > checkpoint step (unsaved progress).

stale.visual: Chips dim to opacity 0.4. Progress bar freezes at last known position. Yellow 'STALE' text (10px) below.

error.visual: Both chips show '--'. Red dashed border. Progress bar hidden.

edge_cases.step_rollover: When step % 500 == 0, progress bar fills completely (100%), then resets to 0% on next tick when cycle increments. Brief full-bar celebration flash (200ms green).
edge_cases.negative_values: Display in red, treat as error state (should never happen — indicates data corruption).
edge_cases.cycle_gap: If checkpoint cycle != current cycle (e.g., after resume with ledger rewind), show a small 'rewound' badge between chips: '↺' (U+21BA).
edge_cases.missing_checkpoint: If organism_latest.json is missing, checkpoint indicator shows gray '?' dot. No checkpoint comparison.

visual_behavior.progress_animation: Progress bar fill uses CSS transition width 1.5s ease-out for smooth step-to-step movement.
visual_behavior.chip_hover: Hovering Cycle chip shows tooltip: 'Cycle boundary every 500 steps. Organ Senate convenes at cycle end.' Hovering Step chip shows: 'Global step counter. Checkpoint saved at step <ckpt_step>.'
visual_behavior.checkpoint_sync_flash: When step reaches a multiple of 100 (checkpoint save point), both chips briefly flash green (300ms) to indicate sync.

CycleStepChip.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'metrics'. Fields: 'cycle', 'step', 'ckpt_cycle', 'ckpt_step'. Updates #cycle-chip and #step-chip inner text, #cycle-progress-bar width, #checkpoint-dot color.

GpuCard.name: GpuCard
GpuCard.purpose: Per-GPU monitoring card showing utilization percentage, memory usage (used/total MiB), and temperature for each installed NVIDIA GPU. The 100M lineage has 2 GPUs (RTX 5060 Ti + RTX 3060).

data_sources.primary: nvidia-smi query via subprocess in Python backend: --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'metrics' → array field 'gpus' with objects: {idx, name, util, mem_used, mem_total, temp}
data_sources.fallback: If nvidia-smi unavailable, psutil for basic GPU detection (limited)

loading.visual: Card skeleton: pulsing bars for util bar, mem bar, and temp. Card labeled 'GPU 0' and 'GPU 1' even while loading (labels from prior known state or config).

live.visual: Card with dark bg (#1a1a1a), rounded corners (8px), padding 16px. Contains:
live.gpu_name: Top-left: GPU name truncated to 28 chars (font: Inter, 12px, color #888888)
live.util_bar: Horizontal bar (width 100%, height 12px, border-radius 6px, bg #333333). Fill: width = util%, color-coded: <70% = #00e676, 70-85% = #ffc107, >85% = #ff1744. Numeric label right-aligned: 'XX%' (font: Cascadia Code, 13px).
live.mem_bar: Horizontal bar similar to util_bar. Fill = mem_used/mem_total * 100. Label: 'XXXX / XXXX MiB'. Color-coded: <70% = #00e676, 70-90% = #ffc107, >90% = #ff1744.
live.temp_indicator: Right side of card: temperature number (font: Cascadia Code, 18px) with °C suffix. Color-coded: <60°C = #00e676, 60-75°C = #ffc107, >75°C = #ff1744. Small thermometer icon (U+1F321) left of number.
live.idle: When util = 0% for > 10s, card gets subtle dimmed overlay (opacity 0.7). 'IDLE' badge appears top-right (font: 10px, bg #333333, text #888888).

stale.visual: All bars freeze at last known position. Card opacity drops to 0.4. Yellow 'STALE' badge.

error.visual: Card shows red dashed border. Text: 'nvidia-smi unavailable' in red. All bars hidden. This is the normal state when no NVIDIA GPU is present or drivers are missing.

oom_warning.visual: Memory bar pulses red (CSS animation: border-color #ff1744, 1s pulse). Red badge 'OOM RISK' appears below memory bar.

edge_cases.no_gpus: Show single card with message: 'No NVIDIA GPUs detected' (gray text, icon: 🖥️). This is expected on CPU-only machines.
edge_cases.single_gpu: Show only one card. Layout adapts: card spans wider.
edge_cases.three_or_more_gpus: Cards wrap to next row. Grid auto-fits.
edge_cases.nvidia_smi_timeout: nvidia-smi can hang (e.g., driver issues). Backend uses subprocess timeout=5. On timeout, show previous values with yellow 'SLOW' badge. Do not block SSE loop.
edge_cases.memory_zero: mem_total=0 or mem_used=0: display '-- / -- MiB'. Bar at 0% width. This can happen during driver reset.
edge_cases.util_over_100: nvidia-smi can report >100% briefly (accounting artifact). Clamp bar to 100% width, show exact value in label with yellow tint.
edge_cases.temp_zero_or_null: Display '--°C' in gray. Some GPUs don't report temperature (e.g., certain Quadro models).
edge_cases.gpu_name_unknown: Display 'GPU <idx>' using the index from nvidia-smi.

visual_behavior.bar_transition: Util and mem bars use CSS transition width 0.8s ease-out.
visual_behavior.temp_color_morph: Temperature color uses CSS transition color 1s ease.
visual_behavior.oom_pulse: CSS keyframe animation: @keyframes oom-pulse { 0%,100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(255,23,68,0.4); } 50% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 6px rgba(255,23,68,0); } }. Runs on loop while OOM condition persists.
visual_behavior.click_expand: Clicking a GPU card expands it to show a small 2-minute utilization sparkline (last 60 data points). Click again to collapse.
visual_behavior.tooltip: Hovering util_bar shows exact timestamp of last nvidia-smi reading.

GpuCard.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'metrics'. Field 'gpus' is an array. Each GpuCard (id='gpu-card-0', 'gpu-card-1') updates its util-bar width, mem-bar width, mem-label text, and temp color independently.

MetricRow.name: MetricRow
MetricRow.purpose: A row in the training metrics panel showing a single scalar metric with its label, current value, delta from the previous reading, and a mini inline sparkline (last 20 values). Collectively, MetricRows form the metrics panel.

data_sources.primary: dopamine_status.txt → respective key for each metric
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'metrics' → all metric fields in a flat object

loading.visual: Row with label text visible, value as pulsing bar (60x16px), sparkline area empty with shimmer.

live.label: Metric name (font: Inter, 11px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.1em, color #888888). Full name on hover tooltip.
live.value: Numeric value (font: Cascadia Code, 18px, color #e0e0e0). Formatted to configured digit count.
live.delta: Change from previous value (font: Cascadia Code, 12px). Arrow prefix: ▲ increase, ▼ decrease. Color: green if moving in 'good' direction, red if 'bad', gray if |delta| < 0.0001.
live.sparkline: Inline SVG sparkline (80x20px) showing last 20 values. Polyline with stroke #00d4ff, stroke-width 1.5, no fill. Y-axis auto-scaled to [min,max] of visible window. X-axis: last 20 points only.
live.perplexity_note: For 'ppl' metric, if loss changes, ppl recomputes as exp(loss). Show both current and previous ppl in delta.

stale.visual: Entire row dims to opacity 0.4. Values frozen. Yellow dot (6px) appears after label.

error.visual: Value shows '--' in red. Sparkline disappears. Label stays visible.

edge_cases.metric_missing: If a key is absent from dopamine_status.txt (e.g., 'gmc' not yet computed), display '--' in gray. Do not show delta. Sparkline shows last available data points (may be shorter than 20).
edge_cases.metric_zero: Display '0.0000' normally. Zero is valid for early training metrics.
edge_cases.metric_negative: Some metrics can legitimately be negative (e.g., delta after loss spike). Display with sign prefix.
edge_cases.delta_overflow: If delta magnitude > 1.0, display delta in yellow with '!' suffix (e.g., '▲ 2.341!') to flag anomalous change.
edge_cases.sparkline_single_point: If only 1 data point available, sparkline shows a single dot (radius 2px) instead of a line.
edge_cases.sparkline_flat: If all values in window are identical (within 0.001), sparkline draws a flat horizontal line at mid-height.

visual_behavior.value_transition: Value text uses CSS transition color 0.3s. No numeric animation (instant update for precision).
visual_behavior.delta_flash: When delta crosses threshold (>0.01 for loss, >0.1 for ppl), delta text briefly scales up (transform: scale(1.2), 300ms) to draw attention.
visual_behavior.sparkline_push: New data point is appended to the right; oldest point drops off the left. The SVG polyline is rebuilt on each update (20 points, negligible cost).
visual_behavior.row_hover: Hovering a row highlights it (bg #222222) and extends the sparkline to show last 60 values via CSS width transition from 80px to 240px on hover.

MetricRow.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'metrics'. Each MetricRow (id='metric-loss', 'metric-ppl', etc.) reads its specific field from the flat metrics object, computes delta client-side, and updates DOM.

ChartCanvas.name: ChartCanvas
ChartCanvas.purpose: Four individual Chart.js line charts arranged in a 2x2 grid showing historical training metrics over the last 4 hours (7200 data points at 2s intervals). Charts: Loss, Perplexity, Tokens/s, Dopamine.

data_sources.primary: Client-side deques (maxlen=7200) per metric, populated from SSE 'metrics' events
data_sources.seed_data: On page load, fetch last 1000 points from SQLite metrics table via GET /api/metrics/history?metric=<key>&limit=1000

ChartCanvas.update_frequency: tier_fast (2s) — data pushed via SSE on each tick. Chart redraw throttled to requestAnimationFrame (~16ms). Chart.update() called with mode 'none' (skip layout/scale recalculation, only redraw data).

loading.visual: Chart area shows skeleton: empty axes with grid lines, title visible, pulsing placeholder in plot area (semitransparent band 30-70% height, opacity animation).

live.visual: Full Chart.js line chart with dark theme.
live.y_auto_scale: Y-axis auto-scales to [min-5%, max+5%] of visible data, clamped to configured y_min/y_max if set.

stale.visual: Last data point shows as a red dot (radius 3px) indicating 'last known value > 30s ago'. Chart area gets subtle red border-left (2px).

error.visual: Chart area shows 'No data available' centered in gray text. Axes visible but empty.

edge_cases.empty_deque: On fresh page load before first SSE event, chart shows seeded data from SQLite. If SQLite also empty, chart shows 'Waiting for training data...' in gray.
edge_cases.single_point: Chart shows a single dot. Line is not drawn (needs >= 2 points). Tooltip still works.
edge_cases.gap_in_data: If no data arrives for > 10s (network blip), chart draws a gap in the line (segment: {borderColor: 'transparent'} for the gap duration). This visually distinguishes 'no data' from 'zero value'.
edge_cases.value_spike: If a value is > 5 standard deviations from the rolling mean, the tooltip marks it with yellow '⚠ anomalous' prefix. Chart still draws the point (no censoring).
edge_cases.browser_tab_background: When tab is hidden (visibilitychange), requestAnimationFrame throttles. On tab focus, chart replays accumulated data points quickly (no animation, instant update to current state).
edge_cases.resize: Chart.js responsive resize is enabled. On container resize, chart redraws. Debounced to 200ms.

visual_behavior.no_flash_morphing: Critical: update chart data arrays in-place (push + shift), then call chart.update('none'). Never destroy/recreate the chart instance. This prevents white-flash on update.
visual_behavior.transition_mode: chart.update() uses transition mode 'default' (0ms duration). For slow-tier data (60s), use 'active' mode (200ms smooth transition) since data rate is lower.
visual_behavior.zoom_hover: Mousing over a chart temporarily expands it (CSS transform: scale(1.05), z-index bump) on hover for 500ms, then returns. Gives a 'focus' effect.
visual_behavior.night_mode_sync: Chart grid/axis colors use CSS custom properties (var(--surface), var(--text-secondary)) so they auto-adapt if theme toggle is added later.

ChartCanvas.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'metrics'. For each chart, client extracts the relevant metric field, appends {x: timestamp, y: value} to the deque, and schedules a throttled chart update. No DOM replacement — Chart.js handles rendering.

BlockchainCard.name: BlockchainCard
BlockchainCard.purpose: Panel showing the status of the causal blockchain: total block count, head hash (truncated), last recorded cycle, and file size. Acts as the integrity anchor for the causal ledger.

data_sources.primary: blocks.jsonl — parsed by Python backend: line count, last line JSON parse for head_hash and cycle, file stat for size_kb
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'blockchain' → fields: blocks, head_hash, last_cycle, size_kb, status

loading.visual: Card with title 'BLOCKCHAIN' visible. Three rows of pulsing bars. Hash truncated placeholder: '0000...' pulsing.

live.block_count: Large number (font: Cascadia Code, 32px, color #00d4ff) with label 'BLOCKS' below.
live.head_hash: 'Head: 3a7f2e1b...' (font: Cascadia Code, 12px, color #888888, first 8 chars of SHA-256).

no_file.visual: Block count shows '0' in gray (#555555). Status line: 'Not recording' (font: Inter, 11px, color #ffc107). Warning icon: ⚠️ (U+26A0). Title dimmed.
no_file.tooltip: 'Blockchain file does not exist. Ensure --blockchain-enabled flag is passed and OrganLedger is initialized.'

empty.visual: Block count shows '0' in gray. Status: 'Empty (awaiting first block)' in yellow.

stale.visual: Card dims to opacity 0.4. Yellow 'STALE' badge. This is expected if training is stopped (no new blocks being written).

error.condition: blocks.jsonl exists but is unparseable (corrupt JSONL)
error.visual: Red dashed border. Status text: 'Parse error' in red. Block count shows last known value or '?'.

edge_cases.blockchain_not_enabled: If config shows blockchain_enabled=false, card shows 'Disabled' with gray icon and tooltip explaining the config toggle. This is the expected state if the flag was not passed.
edge_cases.very_large_file: If blocks.jsonl > 100MB, display size in MB instead of KB. Add yellow note: 'Large file — consider archiving.'
edge_cases.head_hash_mismatch: Backend verifies: last line block_hash should match SHA-256(reconstruct(block)). If mismatch, display red warning: 'Chain integrity check FAILED' with red border. This indicates file corruption or partial write.
edge_cases.rapid_growth: If block count increases by >100 between 10s polls, display block rate: '+XX blocks/s' in green. Normal rate is ~0.5 blocks/s (1 block per step at 2s/step).

visual_behavior.new_block_flash: When block_count increments, the block number briefly pulses (box-shadow cyan, 500ms).
visual_behavior.hash_copy: Clicking the truncated head_hash copies the full SHA-256 to clipboard. Brief 'Copied!' tooltip appears (2000ms).
visual_behavior.expand_detail: Clicking the card expands it to show a mini table of last 5 blocks: [block #, cycle, step, hash truncated]. Collapse on second click.

BlockchainCard.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'blockchain'. Updates #blockchain-card inner content via htmx morph (idiomorph extension for seamless DOM merging). Fields: #block-count, #block-head-hash, #block-cycle, #block-size, #block-status.

OrganChip.name: OrganChip
OrganChip.purpose: A 4x4 grid (16 chips) showing each Darwin-X organ's name and current status. Provides at-a-glance visibility into which biological subsystems are active, dormant, or dead.

data_sources.primary: organism_latest.json → checkpoint file → organ_identity_report.identities (SHA-256 per organ) + organ status from bootstrap.py runtime state
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'organs' → array of {name, status, identity_short, weight_norm, grad_norm_avg}
data_sources.status_determination: Backend checks: (1) organ identity SHA-256 exists in checkpoint → 'active'. (2) organ config toggle disabled → 'disabled'. (3) organ identity missing from checkpoint → 'dormant'. (4) organ known-dead (Curiosity never implemented, Decision Engine writes but nobody reads) → 'dead'. (5) organ recently reanimated by resume hook (e.g., GABA, TTM gates were zero) → 'reanimated'.

OrganChip.update_frequency: tier_slow (60s) — organ status changes rarely (only on checkpoint save or config change)

loading.visual: Grid of 16 chips, each with shimmer animation. Labels visible (from hardcoded list). Status dot hidden.

live.visual: Each chip is a rounded rectangle (bg #1a1a1a, border 1px #333333, padding 8px 12px, min-width 100px).
live.layout: CSS Grid: grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr) on 1080p+. Responsive: repeat(3, 1fr) on tablet, repeat(2, 1fr) on mobile.
live.content: Organ name (font: Inter, 11px, color #e0e0e0) + status dot (10px circle, left of name).

status_colors.dead: #ff1744 (red), dot flat, chip border-color becomes red (1px)
status_colors.reanimated: #b388ff (purple), dot with slow pulse animation (2s cycle, opacity 1.0→0.5→1.0)

stale.visual: All chips dim to opacity 0.4. Status dots freeze at last known color. Yellow 'STALE' badge on grid header.

error.visual: Chips show labels but all dots are gray with '?' inside. Grid header shows 'Organ status unavailable' in red.

edge_cases.organ_not_in_checkpoint: Display as 'dormant' with yellow dot. Tooltip: 'No organ identity found in checkpoint — may not be initialized yet.'
edge_cases.config_toggle_off: Display as 'disabled' with gray dot. Tooltip: '<organ>_enabled: false in config.'
edge_cases.curiosity_permanently_dead: Curiosity chip always shows 'dead' (red) regardless — Curiosity was never implemented in the codebase. Tooltip: 'Curiosity module never implemented. curiosity_enabled key does not exist in DarwinXConfig.'
edge_cases.decision_engine_fantasma: Decision Engine chip shows 'dead' (red) with special tooltip: 'Computes _last_decision_confidence but nobody consumes it. Code exists but output is discarded.'
edge_cases.new_organ_added: If a 17th organ is added to bootstrap.py, the grid auto-adds a new chip. Layout recalculates: 17 mod 4 = 1 extra in last row, centered.
edge_cases.identity_sha256_mismatch: If organ identity SHA-256 in runtime differs from checkpoint, chip border flashes yellow/red alternating (1s cycle). Tooltip: 'Organ weights changed since last checkpoint — unsaved modifications.'

visual_behavior.dot_glow: Active organs have CSS box-shadow glow on their status dot. Dormant/dead do not.
visual_behavior.reanimated_pulse: Reanimated organs use @keyframes reanimated-pulse for subtle pulse to distinguish from normal active.
visual_behavior.chip_hover: Hovering a chip shows a tooltip with: organ full description, status reason, identity SHA-256 truncated (last 16 chars), and last weight/gradient norm if available.
visual_behavior.click_expand: Clicking a chip could (future) show a mini detail panel with full organ metrics. For Wave 3, clicking copies organ name to clipboard.
visual_behavior.grid_loading: On first load, chips appear with staggered fade-in (each chip delayed by 50ms from previous) for visual polish.

OrganChip.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'organs'. The organ grid (#organ-grid) receives an array. Client iterates, updates each chip's status dot color and tooltip text by matching data-name attribute. No full grid replacement — individual chip updates via CSS class toggles.

IntegrityRow.name: IntegrityRow
IntegrityRow.purpose: A row in the integrity panel showing a file's label, its SHA-256 fingerprint (truncated to 16 chars + '...'), and a copy button. Verifies that critical operational files have not been tampered with or corrupted. Five rows total.

data_sources.primary: Python backend computes SHA-256 of each file via hashlib.sha256() with 64KB chunked reading. Results cached for 55s (just under the 60s poll interval).
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'integrity' → object mapping label → {hash_short, hash_full, exists, size_mb, verified_at}

IntegrityRow.update_frequency: tier_slow (60s) — hashing large checkpoint files (~938MB) on every 2s cycle would be I/O expensive

loading.visual: Five rows, each with label visible, hash placeholder as pulsing bar (16 chars wide), copy button dimmed (cursor: wait).

status_icons.verified: Green checkmark (U+2705) — file exists and hash computed successfully
status_icons.not_found: Gray dash (U+2014) — file does not exist at expected path
status_icons.error: Red X (U+274C) — file exists but hash computation failed (I/O error, permissions)

live.hash_format: Font: Cascadia Code, 12px, color #00d4ff. Format: '3a7f2e1b9c4d5f6a...' (first 16 hex chars + '...').
live.copy_button: Small button (24x24px) with clipboard icon (U+1F4CB). On click: copies full SHA-256 (64 hex chars) to clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText().
live.size_hint: After hash: file size in parentheses (font: Inter, 10px, color #666666). E.g., '(938.2 MB)'.
live.verified_at: Rightmost: small timestamp 'Verified 12s ago' (font: Inter, 9px, color #555555) showing time since last hash computation.

stale.visual: Rows dim to opacity 0.4. 'Verified at' timestamp increments (e.g., 'Verified 95s ago'). When > 120s, yellow 'STALE' badge appears.

error.visual: Affected row(s) show red X icon, hash replaced with 'ERROR' in red. Copy button hidden. Tooltip explains error reason.

edge_cases.checkpoint_path_relative: organism_latest.json.path is often a bare filename (e.g., 'organism_cycle_046_step_014500.pt'). Backend resolves relative to CKPT_ROOT. If path is absolute or contains '..', reject and show error.
edge_cases.checkpoint_missing: If checkpoint .pt file does not exist at resolved path, show 'not_found' with tooltip: 'Checkpoint file missing — may have been moved or deleted.'
edge_cases.blocks_jsonl_missing: Expected state when blockchain not recording. Show 'not_found' but with blue info icon (U+2139) instead of red X. Tooltip: 'Blockchain not recording — blocks.jsonl will be created on first block.'
edge_cases.causal_events_missing: Show 'not_found' with yellow warning. Tooltip: 'Causal events file not found — ledger may not have been initialized or was archived.'
edge_cases.hash_mismatch_from_prior: Backend compares current hash with hash from previous poll. If different (file was modified), row border flashes yellow for 2 seconds. Tooltip: 'File modified since last check — previous hash: <old_hash>'.
edge_cases.very_large_file: Checkpoint .pt files can be > 1GB. Hashing takes ~2-3 seconds. Backend uses asyncio.to_thread() to avoid blocking the event loop. During hash, status shows spinner icon (U+23F3) with 'Computing...'.
edge_cases.hash_collision_prefix: Truncated 16-char hash is sufficient for display. Full hash available via copy button. No collision risk in 5 files.

visual_behavior.copy_feedback: On copy button click, button icon changes to checkmark (U+2705) for 1500ms, then reverts to clipboard. Tooltip: 'Copied!' appears briefly.
visual_behavior.hash_change_flash: When a file's hash changes, that row's hash text briefly scales up (transform: scale(1.05), 300ms) and border-left goes yellow (3px).
visual_behavior.row_hover: Hovering a row highlights it (bg #222222) and shows the full hash as a tooltip (64 chars, word-break: break-all).
visual_behavior.section_status: Section header shows aggregate: '5/5 verified' or '4/5 verified, 1 missing' in green/yellow.

IntegrityRow.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'integrity'. Object maps label→data. Client iterates rows (data-integrity-label attribute), updates each row's hash text, status icon, and timestamp. Copy button behavior is purely client-side (no SSE involvement).

AgentTimelineEntry.name: AgentTimelineEntry
AgentTimelineEntry.purpose: A chronological entry in the agent activity timeline showing when a human or AI agent entered or exited the project (from DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md). Provides operational audit trail visibility directly in the dashboard.

data_sources.primary: DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md — parsed by Python backend regex: extracts timestamped blocks with OPERATION, ESTADO ENCONTRADO, AÇÕES, ESTADO DEIXADO
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'timeline' → array of {timestamp, agent, operation_type, summary, entry_type}

AgentTimelineEntry.update_frequency: tier_slow (60s) — DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md changes infrequently (only when an agent works)

loading.visual: Timeline container with 3 skeleton entries: each has pulsing bar for timestamp, pulsing bar for agent name, pulsing bar for summary.

live.visual: Vertical timeline with entries ordered by timestamp (newest at top). Each entry:
live.timeline_line: Vertical line (2px, color #333333) connecting entries. A dot (12px) marks each entry on the line.
live.timestamp: Left of dot: timestamp in UTC (font: Cascadia Code, 10px, color #666666). Format: '07-24 18:30'.
live.agent_name: Right of dot: agent name (font: Inter, 13px, weight 600, color #e0e0e0). E.g., 'Claude (F51 Darwin session)'.
live.operation_dot: Colored dot (8px) left of agent name indicating operation type:
live.summary: Below agent name: one-line summary (font: Inter, 11px, color #888888). First line of the AÇÕES or OBJETIVO field, truncated to 80 chars.
live.expandable: Clicking an entry expands it to show full details: OPERATION, ESTADO ENCONTRADO, AÇÕES, ESTADO DEIXADO, COMMIT, WARNINGS (parsed from the markdown block). Collapse on second click.
live.entry_type_badge: Small badge top-right of entry: 'IN' (green) for ENTRADA, 'OUT' (blue) for SAÍDA, 'IN+OUT' (purple) for combined.

stale.visual: Timeline dims to opacity 0.4. Yellow 'STALE' on header.

error.visual: Timeline shows 'Unable to parse DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md' in red. Last known entries (from cache) still visible but dimmed.

empty.visual: Timeline area shows 'No agent entries yet' in gray italic. This is the state before any agents have worked on the project.

edge_cases.malformed_entry: If a markdown block has missing fields (e.g., no timestamp), show entry with 'Unknown' for missing field in gray italic. Do not skip the entry.
edge_cases.future_timestamp: If timestamp is in the future (clock skew), show with yellow warning icon (U+26A0) and tooltip: 'Timestamp appears to be in the future — possible clock skew.'
edge_cases.duplicate_entry: If two entries have the same timestamp, show both (don't deduplicate — they may be different operations).
edge_cases.very_long_summary: Truncate to 80 chars with '...' suffix. Full text available in expanded view.
edge_cases.no_entries: If DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md has no registered entries (beyond the template), show the template instructions as a gray italic hint: 'No agent entries recorded yet. Agents must register in DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md before working.'
edge_cases.special_characters: Agent names or summaries may contain emoji, Unicode. Display as-is. Font stack (Inter, Cascadia Code) supports Unicode.
edge_cases.cache_stale: If agent_timeline.json cache is older than DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md mtime, backend regenerates cache before sending SSE event.

visual_behavior.new_entry_animation: When a new entry appears (was not in previous poll), it slides in from the top (CSS animation: slideDown 0.4s ease-out, starting from max-height: 0).
visual_behavior.expand_collapse: Expanded detail section uses CSS transition max-height 0.3s ease. Detail content: OPERATION (full text), ESTADO ENCONTRADO (key-value pairs), AÇÕES (numbered list), COMMIT (mono), WARNINGS (yellow-bordered box).
visual_behavior.scroll_position: Timeline container has max-height: 400px with overflow-y: auto. On new entry, if user is scrolled to top, auto-scroll to show new entry. If user has scrolled down to read history, do not auto-scroll (preserve reading position).
visual_behavior.timeline_dot_hover: Hovering the timeline dot enlarges it (12px → 16px) and shows the full UTC timestamp as tooltip.

AgentTimelineEntry.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'timeline'. Array of entries. If the number of entries changed, the entire timeline (#agent-timeline) is rebuilt server-side via Jinja2 template snippet and swapped in via htmx. This is simpler than client-side diffing. The snippet is small (~2KB for 20 entries).

SystemHealthBar.name: SystemHealthBar
SystemHealthBar.purpose: Compact system resource monitor showing RAM usage, disk free space, Python process count, and dashboard uptime. Provides operational awareness of the machine running the training.

data_sources.primary: psutil via Python backend: virtual_memory() for RAM, disk_usage('/') for disk, process_iter() for Python processes, monotonic timer for uptime
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'system' → fields: ram_pct, ram_used_gb, ram_total_gb, disk_pct, disk_free_gb, proc_count, proc_total_mem_gb, uptime_s, dashboard_uptime_s

loading.visual: Four compact bars/labels with pulsing placeholder fills.

live.visual: Horizontal row of 4 compact indicators, each with: label (font: Inter, 9px, uppercase, color #888888), value (font: Cascadia Code, 14px), and a thin progress bar (height: 3px, width: 100%, bg #333333).
live.ram_bar: Fill = ram_pct%. Color: <80% = #00e676, 80-95% = #ffc107, >95% = #ff1744. Label shows 'XX.X / YY.Y GB'.
live.disk_bar: Fill = disk_pct%. Same color thresholds. Label shows 'XXX GB free'.
live.proc_bar: Count of Python processes (font: Cascadia Code, 16px). Color: <2 (dead) = #ff1744, 2-4 (normal) = #00e676, >4 (possible duplicate) = #ffc107. Below: total Python memory in GB.
live.uptime_display: Dashboard uptime in human-readable format: '4h 32m'. Training uptime from training process start time.

stale.visual: All indicators dim. Values freeze. Yellow 'STALE' badge.

error.visual: If psutil unavailable, show 'psutil not installed' in gray with tooltip: 'Install psutil for system health monitoring.'

edge_cases.ram_near_full: When ram_pct > 95%, RAM bar pulses red (same OOM animation as GPU memory). This is critical — OOM killer may terminate the training process.
edge_cases.disk_near_full: When disk_pct > 95%, disk bar pulses red. Checkpoints may fail to save. Warning tooltip: 'Disk nearly full — checkpoint saves may fail.'
edge_cases.python_process_zero: Process count = 0 means training is not running. Display '0' in red with tooltip: 'No Python processes detected — training is stopped.' This should correlate with training_status=stopped.
edge_cases.python_process_many: Process count > 10 may indicate zombie processes from crashed runs. Display count in red with tooltip: 'High process count — possible zombie processes from previous runs.'
edge_cases.uptime_negative: Should never happen (monotonic clock). If it does, display '--' and log error.
edge_cases.uptime_very_long: If uptime > 7 days, display in days: '12d 4h'. Dashboard uptime shown separately in smaller font below.

visual_behavior.bar_transition: Progress bars use CSS transition width 0.8s ease-out.
visual_behavior.critical_pulse: RAM and disk bars use @keyframes critical-pulse when above 95% (same animation as OOM).
visual_behavior.process_count_color: Process count text color uses CSS transition color 1s ease.
visual_behavior.section_compact: This section is intentionally compact (height: ~60px) — it's supportive info, not primary. Sits in the footer or sidebar.

SystemHealthBar.htmx_sse_routing: Listens to SSE event 'system'. Updates #sys-ram-bar width, #sys-ram-text, #sys-disk-bar width, #sys-disk-text, #sys-proc-count, #sys-uptime.

ConnectionStatus.name: ConnectionStatus
ConnectionStatus.purpose: Small persistent indicator in the dashboard header showing whether the SSE connection to the backend is active. Critical for trust in the displayed data — if disconnected, all values are stale.

data_sources.heartbeat: SSE event 'heartbeat' every 15s from server with {server_time: ISO8601}. Client tracks last heartbeat received.
data_sources.secondary: SSE event 'training_status' → field 'status' for running/stopped state

ConnectionStatus.update_frequency: Reactive (no polling — EventSource events drive state)

connecting.condition: EventSource created, connection not yet established
connecting.visual: Yellow pulsing dot (10px, CSS animation: opacity 0.5→1.0→0.5, 1s cycle). Text: 'Connecting...' (font: Inter, 10px, color #ffc107).

connected.condition: EventSource 'open' event fired, heartbeat received within last 20s
connected.visual: Green pulsing dot (10px, CSS glow animation: box-shadow 0 0 8px rgba(0,230,118,0.6), 2s pulse). Text: 'Live' (font: Inter, 10px, color #00e676). On hover: 'SSE connected — data streaming every 2s'.
connected.latency_ms: If heartbeat includes server_time, client computes latency: Date.now() - server_time. Display: 'Live (XXms)' where XX is the round-trip latency.

disconnected.condition: EventSource 'error' event fired, or no heartbeat for > 25 seconds
disconnected.visual: Red solid dot (10px, no glow). Text: 'Disconnected' (font: Inter, 10px, color #ff1744). Below: 'Reconnecting in Xs...' countdown (font: Inter, 9px, color #888888).
disconnected.reconnect_countdown: EventSource auto-reconnects with browser-default backoff (~3s). Client shows countdown to next reconnect attempt based on time since last error.
disconnected.manual_reconnect: Clicking the indicator forces a reconnect: EventSource.close() + new EventSource(url). Useful if browser backoff is too slow.

training_status_indicator.running: Adjacent to connection dot: small green badge 'TRAINING' (bg rgba(0,230,118,0.15), text #00e676).
training_status_indicator.hung: Yellow badge 'HUNG' (bg rgba(255,193,7,0.15), text #ffc107) when training_status=hung. Tooltip: 'No training updates for > 60s — process may be hung.'

edge_cases.initial_connection_fail: If the very first EventSource connection fails (server not running), show 'Server unreachable' in red. Offer a 'Retry' button. Don't show the full dashboard (it would be all stale/error states).
edge_cases.server_restart: If server restarts (SSE reconnects with new connection), all components should re-seed from SQLite history and reset their deques. ConnectionStatus briefly shows 'Reconnected — seeding data...' in yellow.
edge_cases.network_flap: If connection rapidly toggles (connected → disconnected → connected within 5s), suppress the 'Disconnected' text to avoid flicker. Only show 'Disconnected' after 3 consecutive seconds in error state (debounce).
edge_cases.heartbeat_miss: A single missed heartbeat (15s interval) does not trigger disconnect — must miss 2 consecutive heartbeats (30s) before showing disconnected. This tolerates GC pauses or brief network blips.
edge_cases.browser_background: When browser tab is backgrounded, EventSource may buffer events. On tab focus, check last heartbeat timestamp — if > 30s old, show 'Disconnected' briefly then reconnect.

visual_behavior.state_transition: Dot color and text change with CSS transition 0.3s ease.
visual_behavior.training_status_transition: Training status badge morphs with CSS transition background-color 0.5s ease.
visual_behavior.position: Fixed position in the top-right corner of the dashboard header bar (z-index: 100). Always visible regardless of scroll position.

ConnectionStatus.htmx_sse_routing: This component manages the SSE connection itself. It listens to native EventSource events (not SSE event types). It emits connection state changes to a small client-side event bus that other components can subscribe to (e.g., ChartCanvas pauses updates when disconnected). Training status is received via SSE event 'training_status'.

layout_structure.description: CSS Grid layout with named areas. Components are placed into a responsive grid that reflows from 3 columns (1080p) to 4 (1440p+) to 5 (ultrawide).
layout_structure.card_spacing: 16px gap between grid items. Cards have padding: 16px, border-radius: 8px.

file_plan.src/tools/darwin_dashboard_web.py: FastAPI app, SSE endpoint, data collectors (asyncio polling loop), logbook parser, SQLite WAL manager. Main entry point.
file_plan.src/tools/templates/dashboard.html: Single Jinja2 template. Full HTML document with CSS Grid layout, embedded <style> for critical CSS, links to external static files.
file_plan.src/tools/static/htmx.min.js: htmx 2.x (14KB). Committed to repo for offline capability. Loaded via <script src> without integrity hash (local file).
file_plan.src/tools/static/dashboard.css: Dark theme CSS custom properties, component styles, responsive grid, animations. Non-critical CSS loaded via <link>.
file_plan.workspace/runtime/dashboard/metrics.db: SQLite WAL database (auto-created on first run). Tables: metrics, gpu_snapshots, checkpoint_history.
file_plan.workspace/runtime/dashboard/runs.jsonl: Training run log (start/stop events appended by dashboard).

python_backend_modules.DataCollector: Async class polling source files every 2s. Reads mtime+size, parses deltas, pushes to asyncio.Queue. Three queues: fast_queue (2s), medium_queue (10s), slow_queue (60s).
python_backend_modules.SSEManager: Manages connected SSE clients. On new data in queue, broadcasts SSE event to all clients. Handles client disconnect cleanup.
python_backend_modules.LogbookParser: Regex parser for DIARIO_DE_BORDO.md. Extracts ESTADO ATUAL table, agent entries, bugs section. Caches parsed result. File lock (msvcrt.locking on Windows) for writes.
python_backend_modules.DatabaseManager: SQLite WAL manager. Inserts metrics and GPU snapshots on each poll. Provides history queries for chart seeding. Auto-vacuums on dashboard startup.
python_backend_modules.HashCache: Computes SHA-256 of 5 integrity files with TTL caching. Uses asyncio.to_thread() for hashing to avoid event loop blocking.

client_side_state.deques: Four Float64Arrays (ring buffers, maxlen=7200) for loss, ppl, tok_s, dopamine. Paired with timestamp Int32Arrays.
client_side_state.previous_metrics: Object storing last received metrics for delta computation (MetricRow, HeroLoss trend).
client_side_state.connection_state: Enum: connecting | connected | disconnected. Updated by ConnectionStatus component.
client_side_state.organ_states: Array of 16 {name, status, identity_short} objects. Updated on 'organs' SSE event.
client_side_state.training_status: Enum: running | stopped | hung | unknown. Updated on 'training_status' SSE event.

ssr_initial_load.description: On first page load (HTTP GET /), the Jinja2 template renders with server-side data seeded from the latest poll. This prevents a 'flash of loading skeletons' and ensures the dashboard is immediately useful.
seeded_data: Current loss, cycle, step from latest dopamine_status.txt
Last 1000 data points per chart from SQLite metrics table
ssr_initial_load.after_load: Browser establishes SSE connection. First SSE event triggers differential update (only changed values replace DOM). Charts receive incremental data points beyond the seeded 1000.
